name: ATF_TC_BODY(recvfrom_success, tc)
prose: Generated function recvfrom_success_body(tc), produced by ATF_TC_BODY(recvfrom_success, tc). Takes the ATF test case pointer and returns void. It fills the server address with assign_address, requires a PF_UNIX SOCK_DGRAM socket and a bind of it to that address to succeed, requires a second datagram socket and a sendto of the message buffer to the server address not to return -1, starts auditing with setup(fds, auclass), then requires recvfrom on the server socket not to return 0 (a return of -1 would pass this check), builds the regex "recvfrom.*0x<sockfd>.*return,success,<bytes>" from the descriptor and the received byte count, calls check_audit with it and closes both sockets with close_sockets. A failing ATF_REQUIRE ends the test case before the later steps.
note: Read network.c:788-812. Reviewer round 15 right: the check is "!= 0", so a -1 return does not stop the test (802-803).

name: FORK_TEST(Fcntl, Basic)
prose: Generated function Fcntl_Basic_ForkTest(), the body of FORK_TEST(Fcntl, Basic) (the macro makes a gtest case Fcntl.BasicForked that runs this function in a forked child). Takes no arguments, returns void, reports failures through non-fatal gtest expectations. It opens /etc/passwd read-only, creates a PF_LOCAL stream socket and a shared-memory object /capsicum-test-<uid> (the SHM entry is dropped when shm_open fails with ENOSYS), and creates for each of them a dup limited to CAP_READ and CAP_FCNTL, storing it in the caps map (that map is not used again). It enters capability mode, then for each raw descriptor expects fcntl(F_GETFL) to succeed, dups it, limits the dup to CAP_READ only and expects fcntl(F_GETFL) on that dup to fail with -1 and errno ENOTCAPABLE, and closes that dup. Finally it closes the raw descriptors (the dups in caps are not closed) and unlinks the shared-memory name.
note: Read fcntl.cc:22-73 and the FORK_TEST macro (capsicum-test.h:109-119). Reviewers right: round 15 (F_GETFL is not tested on the CAP_FCNTL-limited descriptors, the caps map is never used afterwards: 52-53 copies files into all, 60-68), round 17 (the dups in caps are never closed, 69-71).

name: TEST(Linux, fstatat)
prose: Generated gtest body Linux_fstatat_Test::TestBody(), from TEST(Linux, fstatat); takes no arguments, returns void, failures are non-fatal expectations. It creates the file "cap_fstatat" (O_CREAT|O_RDWR) in the temporary directory, writes 4 bytes, makes a dup limited to CAP_READ|CAP_FSTAT and a dup limited to CAP_READ, and expects fstatat(fd, "", AT_EMPTY_PATH) and the CAP_FSTAT dup to succeed and the CAP_READ-only dup to fail with ENOTCAPABLE; it closes those descriptors. It then opens the temporary directory read-only, makes dir_rf, a dup of it limited to CAP_READ|CAP_FSTAT, and dir_ro as dup(fd) of the descriptor number that was just closed (so dir_ro duplicates whatever now has that number, normally the directory descriptor just opened, and fails if the number is not open), limited to CAP_READ, and repeats the three fstatat expectations with the name "cap_fstatat" and AT_EMPTY_PATH, closes the directory descriptors and unlinks the file.
note: Read linux.cc:330-370. Reviewer round 15 right that dir_ro is a dup of the already closed fd (357), so that part of the test depends on descriptor reuse; it does not necessarily fail.

name: FORK_TEST_ON_MQ(PosixMqueue, CapModeIfMqOpenAvailable, "/cap_mq")
prose: Generated function PosixMqueue_CapModeIfMqOpenAvailable_ForkTest(), the body of FORK_TEST_ON_MQ(PosixMqueue, CapModeIfMqOpenAvailable, "/cap_mq") (the macro makes a gtest case that runs this function in a forked child and then unlinks the queue name). Takes no arguments and returns void. If mq_open of "/cap_mq" fails with ENOSYS it calls GTEST_SKIP and returns. Otherwise it expects the open to succeed, makes dups limited to CAP_READ, CAP_WRITE and CAP_EVENT, closes the original queue descriptor, installs a SIGUSR2 handler that sets a flag and enters capability mode. It expects mq_open of a new name to fail with the capability-mode error, mq_notify to succeed on the CAP_EVENT dup and fail with ENOTCAPABLE on the read and write dups, mq_timedsend to succeed on the write dup and fail ENOTCAPABLE on the read dup, sleeps one second and expects the signal flag set, expects mq_getattr and mq_setattr to succeed on the CAP_EVENT dup and only mq_getattr to fail ENOTCAPABLE on the write dup (mq_setattr is not tried on the other dups), expects mq_timedreceive to fail ENOTCAPABLE on the write dup and succeed on the read dup returning the message "xyzzy" with priority 10, and closes the three dups.
note: Read mqueue.cc:16-99. Reviewer round 15 right: only mq_getattr_ is tested negatively (86), not mq_setattr_. Failures are non-fatal expectations.

It reads CLOCK_REALTIME into current_time, registers reset_time with atexit, sets the clock to that same time (the test is skipped when the clock cannot be set), creates a CLOCK_REALTIME timerfd and arms it with an absolute TIME_T_MAX expiry and TFD_TIMER_CANCEL_ON_SET, starts clock_change_thread, requires two consecutive reads of the timerfd each to fail with errno ECANCELED, joins the thread and requires close(tfd) to return 0. clock_change_thread sets the clock to current_time, then waits 2 seconds and sets it again with the time advanced by 2 seconds. A failing ATF_REQUIRE fails the test.

name: ATF_TC_BODY(timerfd_root__advance_time_no_cancel, tc)
prose: Generated function timerfd_root__advance_time_no_cancel_body(tc), produced by ATF_TC_BODY(timerfd_root__advance_time_no_cancel, tc). Takes the ATF test case pointer (unused) and returns void. It creates a CLOCK_REALTIME timerfd (required to succeed), reads the current time, registers reset_time with atexit, and arms the timerfd with a one-shot absolute expiry 10 seconds ahead and no cancel-on-set flag. It advances current_time by 9 seconds and sets the clock to it (the test is skipped if setting the clock is not allowed), then lowers the saved current_time by 8 seconds, polls the timerfd for up to 1800 ms and requires exactly one ready descriptor, requires read to return 8 bytes with an expiration count of 1, and requires close to return 0. A failing ATF_REQUIRE fails the test.
